subject: POC success criteria & integration plan — Redwood x Novabyte
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Torres <ev.torres@novabyte.ai>, Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@novabyte.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC success criteria & integration plan — Redwood x Novabyte

Hi Evelyn / Arjun —

Thanks again for a great discovery call earlier. Quick recap + a proposed POC plan so we can move to a short trial: please review and flag anything that’s missing.

POC scope (proposed)
- Integrate Redwood inference for: document summarization + entity extraction pipeline (streaming responses for summaries).
- Evaluate both hosted API and a short Dedicated pilot for redaction-sensitive flows.

Success criteria (what Novabyte wants to validate)
1) Latency: median generation latency below 250ms for 512-token requests; p95 < 800ms under baseline load.
2) Throughput: sustain 80 QPS with average sequence length ~400 tokens.
3) Cost: expected inference cost per 1k tokens <= target threshold (we'll sync on a target after you share expected call volume).
4) Quality: extract/summary F1 >= 0.82 on the provided eval set; no data leakage; function-calling results match schema.
5) Reliability: fewer than 0.5% model failures / errors during a 2-week run.

Technical evaluation plan
- SE-led integration session (30–60m) to walk SDK + streaming setup.
- We’ll provide a small eval harness and a set of 250 prompt/response pairs for automated scoring.
- Run A/B against your current baseline (same prompts, blind scoring).

Integration highlights (what we’ll test)
- SDK: quickstart snippet (we’ll send a sample) to integrate /v1/generate and /v1/stream endpoints.
- Streaming: SSE or chunked JSON responses for progressive summary rendering.
- Function calling: validate JSON schema-based calls for redaction and downstream tooling.
- KV cache/prefix caching: test warm-start for repeated document prefixes to measure token savings.

Owners and timeline (proposed)
- Novabyte tech lead: Evelyn Torres (deliver demo dataset + security questionnaire).
- Redwood SE: Marcus Lin (integration + streaming session).
- Redwood AE: Soojin Lee (program owner, milestone tracking).
- Kickoff: Mar 20, SE session: Mar 22, dataset delivery: Mar 24, POC end: Apr 14.

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.pdf (POC checklist), sdk-sample-snippets.md (short code examples).

Next steps
1) Confirm timeline and owners.
2) Share the demo dataset and SOC2 contact (for procurement).
3) Marcus will schedule the SE integration session — propose Mar 22 or Mar 23.

If that all looks good I’ll calendar the SE slot and drop the HubSpot mutual action plan link.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Torres <ev.torres@novabyte.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@novabyte.ai>
Date: 2027-03-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & integration plan — Redwood x Novabyte

Thanks Soojin — this looks like a solid starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: we have a product launch in early May; can we compress the POC window by starting the SE session next week and move the POC end to Apr 7 if initial runs look promising?
- Security: our security team needs SOC 2 evidence and a short CNAPP checklist before we share any production data. I’ve CC’d security@novabyte.ai.
- Dedicated capacity: for PII redaction flows we’d prefer to test on a Dedicated instance for the trial days. Can Redwood provide a short quote for a 4-week Dedicated reservation?

I’ve attached a small sample of our demo dataset (Novabyte-demo-dataset.csv).

Evelyn
VP Product, Novabyte

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Torres <ev.torres@novabyte.ai>, Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@novabyte.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & integration plan — Redwood x Novabyte

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the sample and timeline note. A few technical clarifications and what we’ll demo in the SE session: 

1) Streaming behavior: Redwood supports SSE chunked streaming and a short-poll streaming endpoint. Example workflow: open /v1/stream with stream=true and receive chunked JSON delta events. You can render partial summaries as tokens arrive.
2) Auth & isolation: for Dedicated we provision a customer-dedicated GPU pool and a private API key scoped to that pool. For Private/VPC deployments we can integrate your KMS and IP allowlist.
3) Function calling: we’ll demonstrate a function schema where model emits a single JSON payload: {"action":"redact","fields":["name","ssn"]}. We’ll provide 2 example schemas in the session.
4) Batching & cache knobs: suggested starting configs — batch_size: 8, max_tokens_per_request: 1024, kv_cache_enabled: true (for repeated-doc flows). We’ll show how these affect latency vs cost.

Quick asks for sizing before the session: 
- Expected peak concurrent QPS (approx).
- Typical input sequence length distribution (min/median/p95).

I’ll include simple curl + SDK snippets in the deck for the SE demo.

On the Dedicated quote: Soojin, I can draft a short estimate for a 4-week reservation and include burst capacity options.

—Marcus
Senior SE, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Torres <ev.torres@novabyte.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@novabyte.ai>, security@novabyte.ai
Date: 2027-03-18T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & integration plan — Redwood x Novabyte

Thanks Marcus — a couple quick answers: 
- Peak: ~120 QPS for ingestion at peak days, but sustained average ~40 QPS.
- Sequence lengths: min ~50 tokens, median ~380 tokens, p95 ~1100 tokens.

Function calling: we do want to keep the structured function-calling flow so our downstream pipeline can automatically accept redaction decisions. I’m attaching an example-function-schema.json that shows the expected shape.

Security: our team will send a short set of control questions; please route SOC2 evidence to security@novabyte.ai.

If you can update the timeline to start SE session on Mar 22 and shorten the POC window to end Apr 7 (accelerated), we’ll prioritize resource allocation on our side.

Best,
Evelyn

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Evelyn / Arjun — thanks for the timing and the data points. Confirming what we agreed and next steps now that we have sizing: 

Confirmed changes
- SE session: Mar 22 (Marcus to send calendar invite; 45m).
- POC window: Mar 22 -> Apr 7 (accelerated).
- Dedicated pilot: Redwood will provide a 4-week Dedicated reservation quote (So0jin will send a commercial note + estimated cost by EOD Mar 23).

Action owners
- Novabyte: deliver full demo dataset + security contact (Evelyn) by Mar 24.
- Redwood SE: integration session + sample SDK snippets (Marcus) on Mar 22.
- Redwood AE: finalize mutual-action-plan & dedicated quote (Soojin) by Mar 23.

Milestones
- Mar 22: Kickoff + SE integration demo (Marcus).
- Mar 24: Dataset + security questionnaire received.
- Mar 25–31: Initial runs, automated scoring against eval set.
- Apr 5–7: Final validation & wrap.

Temporary test config we’ll start with (can tune after initial runs):
- endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
- streaming: https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?stream=true
- sdk: python redwood.Client(api_key=...); client.generate(..., max_tokens=1024, batch_size=8, kv_cache=True)
- function-calling: include schema in request; expect JSON action payload in response.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAA + milestones). I’ll send the Dedicated quote and HubSpot link after this email.

Thanks — looking forward to the SE session.

Best,
